title: Present Simple or Continuous?
instructions: Completá con la forma correcta del verbo entre paréntesis.
text:
1. She usually [1] (work) in the office, but this week she [2] (work) from home.
2. Look! The build [3] (fail) again.
3. Our team [4] (deploy) to production every Friday.
4. Water [5] (boil) at 100 degrees.
5. I [6] (not / use) Windows at work. I use Linux.
6. A: Where's Sam? B: He [7] (talk) to the client at the moment.

pat: this week marca una situación temporal → Continuous: is working.
'Look!' indica que pasa ahora → Continuous: is failing.
every Friday marca una rutina → Present Simple.
es una verdad general → Present Simple.
items.e: Verdad general → Present Simple; water = it → boils.

pat: la negación del Simple es don't + verbo base: don't use. am not using mezcla aspectos.
la negación del Present Simple necesita el auxiliar: don't use.
items.e: Negativo de Present Simple → don't + verbo base.

title: Present Perfect: Simple or Continuous?
instructions: Completá con la forma correcta del verbo entre paréntesis.
text:
1. I [1] (already / fix) the bug.
2. I [2] (debug) this function for three hours and I still can't find the problem.
3. [3] (you / ever / deploy) to a live server?
4. We [4] (know) each other for ten years.
5. He [5] (finish) the report. You can read it now.
6. How long [6] (you / wait) for the build?
7. I [7] (see) that error yesterday.

pat: el Perfecto lleva have + participio: have already fixed.
for three hours (duración hasta ahora) → have been debugging.
items.e: 'for three hours' + sigue sin resolverse → foco en la duración: have been + -ing.

pat: mezcla do (Simple) con ever (experiencia, Perfecto): Have you ever deployed?
pregunta de Perfecto: Have + sujeto + participio (Have you ever deployed?).
items.e: 'ever' → experiencia de vida → Have + sujeto + participio.

pat: know es un verbo de estado: no admite forma continua. Con for/since + período va Present Perfect SIMPLE (have known).
for five years es un período ABIERTO que llega hasta ahora → Present Perfect (have known), no Present Simple.
knowed no existe: know es irregular → knew → known. Después de have va el participio: have known.
items.e: know es state verb + 'for' → Present Perfect Simple, NO Continuous (Unit1/01).

pat: falta el auxiliar: has finished (resultado presente).
items.e: Resultado presente (ya se puede leer). He → has + participio.

pat: How long pide duración hasta ahora → have you been waiting.
yesterday es un momento CERRADO del pasado → Past Simple. El Present Perfect es para períodos ABIERTOS hasta ahora (for, since, so far).
saw es el pasado, no el participio: see → saw → seen (have + seen).
Y aun corrigiendo la forma (have seen), yesterday es un momento CERRADO → Past Simple: I saw.
items.e: 'yesterday' es un momento CERRADO → Past Simple. Present Perfect es para períodos ABIERTOS hasta ahora (for, since, so far).

title: Questions and negatives: one auxiliary per aspect
instructions: Completá con la pregunta o negación correcta. Recordá: cada aspecto tiene un único auxiliar.
text:
1. [1] (she / work) remotely?
2. She [2] (not / work) on Fridays.
3. [3] (you / finish) the task yet?
4. I [4] (not / finish) yet.
5. [5] (he / study) right now?
6. They [6] (not / use) the old server at the moment.

pat: después de does el verbo va en base: does she work.
'Is she working remotely?' es válida en inglés (trabajo en curso), pero la consigna pide la pregunta de Present Simple: Does she work remotely?
en una pregunta el auxiliar va primero: Does she work...?
items.e: Present Simple: Do/Does + sujeto + verbo BASE.

pat: después de doesn't el verbo va en base: doesn't work.
mezcla auxiliares (does + is): cada aspecto tiene el suyo.
she → doesn't (don't es para I / you / we / they), y 'not' solo no alcanza.
items.e: She → doesn't + verbo base (nunca doesn't works).

pat: ^do you have finished$|^do you finish$|^did you finish$
yet + participio = Perfecto: Have you finished...? (nunca do + have).
^does he is studying$|^does he studying$|^does he study$
'right now' pide Continuo: Is he studying? does es del Simple.
items.e: 'right now' → Continuo → Is + sujeto + -ing. Nunca does + is.

pat: 'at the moment' pide Continuo: aren't using.

title: State verbs (and their exceptions)
instructions: Completá con la forma correcta. Ojo: algunos verbos de estado no admiten -ing.
text:
1. I [1] (know) the answer.
2. She [2] (not / understand) this error message.
3. We [3] (know) our client for five years.
4. Right now I [4] (have) lunch.
5. I [5] (have) two laptops.
6. She usually ignores emails, but today she [6] (be) very helpful.
7. I [7] (think) about changing jobs.

pat: know es verbo de estado: nunca va en continuo → know.
items.e: know = state verb → nunca en continuo.

pat: understand es verbo de estado: no va en continuo → doesn't understand.
después de doesn't va la base: doesn't understand.
items.e: understand = state verb → Present Simple negativo.

pat: know es un verbo de estado: no admite forma continua. Con for/since + período va Present Perfect SIMPLE (have known).
for five years es un período ABIERTO que llega hasta ahora → Present Perfect (have known), no Present Simple.
knowed no existe: know es irregular → knew → known. Después de have va el participio: have known.
El sujeto es We → have known. has es solo para he / she / it.
items.e: State verb + for → Present Perfect Simple.

pat: Acá have = 'almorzar' (una acción), no 'tener': por eso admite continuo, y 'Right now' lo confirma → am having.
Acá have = 'tener' (posesión): es un verbo de estado y no va en continuo, aunque se hable del presente → have.
be en simple describe cómo ES ella normalmente. Con 'today' y un comportamiento inusual se usa is being (está siendo, actúa distinto hoy).
items.e: be + comportamiento temporal/inusual → is being (She is kind → She's being kind today).

pat: think = 'opinar' va en simple (I think it's wrong). Acá es 'estar considerando' (proceso mental en curso) → am thinking.
items.e: think = 'considerar' (proceso mental en curso) → admite -ing. 'I think it's wrong' (opinión) sería simple.
items.altnote: Válida en inglés real (por ejemplo, 'I've been thinking about it for weeks'), pero el ejercicio pide 'am thinking' porque no hay ninguna marca de duración (for, since, lately): sin ese dato, lo más simple es un proceso mental en curso ahora. En el examen, si aparece for/since/lately, el Perfect Continuous sí sería la respuesta.

title: ¿Qué tiempo es?
instructions: Elegí el tiempo verbal de la parte en negrita.

Present Continuous: tiempo
every Friday es una rutina; el Continuous es para lo que pasa ahora o es temporal.
Present Perfect Simple: el Perfecto lleva have / has + participio; deploy está en forma base.
Present Perfect Continuous: el Perfect Continuous lleva have been + -ing.
Imperative: hay sujeto (I): el imperativo no lo lleva.

items.q: I **have been debugging** this for two hours.

Present Simple: hay have been + -ing, no un verbo base.
Present Continuous: forma
el Continuous sería am / is / are + -ing; acá hay have been (duración).
Present Perfect Simple: el Simple sería have debugged; acá hay been + -ing y for two hours (foco en la duración).
Imperative: hay sujeto y auxiliares: no es un imperativo.

Present Simple: has + participio es Perfecto, no Simple.
Present Continuous: forma
el Continuous sería is pushing; acá hay has + participio.
Present Perfect Continuous: falta been + -ing; has just pushed es el Perfecto simple.
Imperative: hay sujeto (She): no es un imperativo.

Present Simple: right now marca una acción en curso → Continuous.
Present Perfect Simple: is + -ing es Continuous; el Perfecto lleva has / have + participio.
Imperative: hay sujeto (The server): no es un imperativo.

Present Simple: sin sujeto y con Don't es un imperativo negativo; el Simple negativo llevaría sujeto (She doesn't push).
Present Continuous: forma
el Continuous lleva am / is / are + -ing.

items.q: We **are working** on a Python project this week.

Present Simple: this week marca una situación temporal → Continuous.
Imperative: hay sujeto (We): no es un imperativo.

items.e: 'ever' → experiencia. La forma es Have you ... used.

Present Simple: Have + sujeto + participio es una pregunta de Perfecto, no de Simple.
Present Continuous: forma
el Continuous sería Are you using...?
Present Perfect Continuous: el Continuous perfecto llevaría been + -ing; used solo (Have you ever used) es el Perfecto simple (experiencia).

Present Continuous: tiempo
es una verdad general, no algo que pasa ahora.
Present Perfect Simple: falta has / have: boils solo es Simple.
Imperative: hay sujeto (Water): no es un imperativo.

items.q: How long **have you been learning** React?

Present Simple: hay have you been + -ing (duración), no un verbo base.
Present Continuous: tiempo
How long pide duración hasta ahora → Perfect Continuous.
Present Perfect Simple: How long pide duración: hace falta been + -ing.

title: Imperativo o Present Simple: ¿hay sujeto?
instructions: Elegí qué es la parte en negrita. Pista de tus apuntes: ¿tiene sujeto explícito?

Present Simple: no hay sujeto: es un imperativo (instrucción directa). El Simple llevaría sujeto (She opens).
Present Continuous: forma
el Continuous lleva am / is / are + -ing.
forma
opens no lleva is + -ing, y every day marca una rutina.
Imperative: hay sujeto (She): el imperativo no lo lleva.

items.q: **Check** the logs if the build fails.

Present Simple: sin sujeto → imperativo. El Simple llevaría sujeto.
Present Continuous: forma
el Continuous lleva am / is / are + -ing.

items.e: Con sujeto + doesn't → Present Simple negativo.

Present Continuous: forma
doesn't + base es el negativo del Simple; el Continuous sería isn't pushing.
Imperative: hay sujeto (She) y doesn't: el imperativo negativo es Don't sin sujeto.

items.q: **Don't commit** without running the tests first.

Present Simple: sin sujeto previo, Don't + base = imperativo negativo. El Simple negativo llevaría sujeto.
Present Continuous: forma
el Continuous lleva am / is / are + -ing.

Imperative: hay sujeto y auxiliar is: no es un imperativo.

title: Imperatives: escribí la instrucción
instructions: Completá con el imperativo (afirmativo o negativo) del verbo entre paréntesis.
text:
1. [1] (not / touch) the production database.
2. [2] (run) the migration before deploying.
3. Please [3] (restart) the server.
4. [4] (not / be) late for the stand-up meeting.

pat: el imperativo negativo es Don't + verbo base.
después de Don't va la base: don't touch.
el imperativo no lleva sujeto ni -s: run.

title: Discrete cloze: presentes mezclados
instructions: Elegí la opción correcta para cada oración.

for: for va con una DURACIÓN (for ten years). 2019 es un punto de inicio → since.
from: from...to marca un rango; con Present Perfect y un punto de inicio se usa since.

items.q: We have known each other ___ ten years.

since: since necesita un punto de inicio (since 2015). ten years es una duración → for.
during: during + un evento (during the meeting). Una duración con Present Perfect va con for.

items.q: I ___ him at the office yesterday.
items.e: 'yesterday' es un momento CERRADO → Past Simple.

have seen: yesterday es un momento CERRADO → Past Simple. Present Perfect es para períodos abiertos hasta ahora.
have been seeing: Present Perfect (Continuous) tampoco combina con yesterday, y además see (ver) no suele ir en continuo.

items.q: She ___ the answer, so she never asks.

isn't knowing: know es un verbo de estado: no admite continuo.
doesn't knows: Después de doesn't el verbo va en base: doesn't know.

Do: yet + finished (participio) indica Perfecto → Have you finished. do es del Simple y pediría Do you finish.
Are: Are va con -ing (Are you finishing?) o con pasiva; acá hay un participio con yet: Perfecto → Have.

items.e: Con el verbo to be, el adverbio de frecuencia va DESPUÉS: is always.

always is: Con el verbo to be el adverbio va DESPUÉS (is always). Antes del verbo va con los verbos comunes (He always works).
is being always: is being describe un comportamiento temporal o inusual; acá es una costumbre → is always.

items.q: They ___ on a new feature this week.

work: this week marca una situación TEMPORAL, no una rutina → Continuous (are working).
have worked: Es gramaticalmente posible (this week es un período abierto), pero enfoca el resultado. La oración habla de un trabajo en curso y temporal → are working.

items.q: Do you like this design? ___ OK?
items.e: look (= parecer) es verbo de percepción/estado → Present Simple. Pregunta: Does + it + look.

Is it looking: 'Is it looking OK?' existe, pero se usa para un cambio en curso ('how is it looking?'). Acá se pregunta cómo se VE algo: look (= parecer) va en simple → Does it look OK?
Does it looks: Después de does el verbo va en base: Does it look.

Después de doesn't el verbo vuelve a la forma base: doesn't work. El -s de he/she/it ya lo lleva doesn't.
La negación del Present Simple necesita el auxiliar: doesn't work. 'not' solo no alcanza.

Mezcla auxiliares: do (Simple) + have (Perfecto). El Perfecto usa solo have/has: I haven't finished.
didn't ya marca el pasado: el verbo va en base (didn't finish).
Y aun corregida, sería Past Simple; acá se busca el Present Perfect (I haven't finished).

Does she is working?: Mezcla auxiliares: does (Simple) + is (Continuo). Cada aspecto tiene el suyo: Is she working?
Does she working?: Con does el verbo va en base (Does she work?). Para el Continuo el auxiliar es is: Is she working?

know es un verbo de estado: no admite continuo → I know.
Falta el auxiliar (am) y, aun con él, know no va en continuo → I know.

yesterday es un momento CERRADO → Past Simple. La forma have seen es correcta, pero no combina con yesterday.
saw es el pasado, no el participio: see → saw → seen (have + seen).
Y aun corrigiendo la forma (have seen), yesterday es un momento CERRADO → Past Simple: I saw him yesterday.

o: I have been working here since 2020.
items.a: I have been working here since 2020.
items.e: since + punto de inicio → Present Perfect (Continuous).

since + un punto de inicio en el pasado que llega hasta ahora pide Present Perfect (have been working). am working no se combina con since.
El Present Simple no expresa duración desde un punto del pasado; con since va Present Perfect.

o: Have you finished it last week?
Did you finish it last week?
Do you finished it last week?
items.a: Did you finish it last week?

Have you finished it last week?: last week es un momento CERRADO → Past Simple (Did you finish...?). El Present Perfect es para períodos abiertos hasta ahora.
Do you finished it last week?: Después de do/did el verbo va en base, no en pasado (finish).
Y do es presente: last week pide did → Did you finish it last week?

o: The windows have cleaned every week.
The windows are cleaned every week.
items.a: The windows are cleaned every week.
items.e: Las ventanas RECIBEN la acción → pasiva: be + participio.

Las ventanas no limpian: RECIBEN la acción → pasiva con be (are cleaned), no con have.
Falta el auxiliar y con -ing no es pasiva. La pasiva es be + participio: are cleaned.

items.e: Adverbio de frecuencia antes del verbo principal (always yells).

Los adverbios de frecuencia (always, never, usually) van ANTES del verbo principal: He always yells.
Con he/she/it el Present Simple lleva -s: yells.

Falta el verbo to be: She is a developer.
She → is. are es para you / we / they.
